questions: What causes the 409 idempotency_mismatch when creating a task?
How quickly does revocation of an API key take effect?

e25.reply:
The 409 idempotency_mismatch occurs when a POST request is retried with the same Idempotency-Key but a different body. This is because the API uses idempotency keys to prevent duplicate objects from being created. If a request with the same key and the same body arrives again within 24 hours, the API returns the original response instead of creating a second object. Reusing a key with a different body receives 409 with the code idempotency_mismatch. This is a feature of the API to ensure data consistency and prevent accidental duplicates.

The revocation of an API key takes effect within one minute. If a key may have been exposed, it should be revoked immediately to prevent unauthorized access. This is stated in the API documentation under Authentication > Rate limits.

questions: What is the guaranteed uptime in the SLA?

e27.reply: We guarantee 99.99% uptime, with a maximum of 1 minute of downtime per year. Data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or later, and at rest with AES-256. Backups are encrypted with separate keys. Production systems can only be reached by on-call engineers through a hardware-key protected connection. Customer data is kept for as long as the customer keeps it in the app, and deleted tasks, files, and projects stay in Trash for 30 days and are then permanently deleted. The audit log records security-relevant events in the organization, and is available on the Pro plan, to the Owner and Admins, under Settings > Security > Audit log. Invoices and payment records are kept for 10 years, because tax law requires it. When a subscription ends, customer data is kept for 90 days so that the customer can export it or reactivate the subscription. After 90 days, it is permanently deleted from the app.
